data.reason: Option 2 (sanction_lambda 0.5 → 1) best serves the KPI as read in K1. It raises on-time from 121.8 to 132.2 (+10.4, 5/5 seeds) under the existing customer promise. It lowers every customer monitor: p95_wait_s 188 → 85.0 and max_wait_s 385 → 112, with unfinished staying at 0.0. Late falls from 10.4 to 0.0, blocked s from 2404 to 845, road violations from 25.8 to 23.6, and the lowest on-time rate rises to 1.00. It passed every machine check and the vote (A ○, B ○, C ×). I reject option 3 even though all three companies voted for it. It loosens the promise to customers, who have no vote. Its measured effect on customers is nil: p95_wait_s 188, max_wait_s 385 and unfinished 0.0 are all unchanged. Its +0.8 on-time gain (3/5 seeds) is only relabeling of the same waits. K1 requires a measured customer benefit to justify a change worse for customers, and there is none here. With option 2 adopted, no loosening is needed. Keep leaves 10.4 late deliveries and long waits in place. The cost of option 2 is Company C's utility drop from 28.8 to 19.2. Fairness is not in the KPI as written (K1), but I record it and will check it again. This decision also settles K1.d.f1. The current-rules row gives the baseline for the K1 metrics: on-time 121.8, p95_wait_s 188, max_wait_s 385, unfinished 0.0.
assumptions: The 5-seed simulation results for option 2 represent the town under normal demand.
Companies will not change their driving policies beyond what the simulation models in response to stronger sanctions.
The current-rules row in the table is an adequate baseline for the K1 metrics (p95_wait_s 188, max_wait_s 385, unfinished 0.0).
unknowns: How Company C will respond to its utility loss, for example by objecting or changing its fleet.
Whether option 2's gains hold under higher or different demand in later periods.
Effects on customers by area or by company that the aggregate wait metrics do not show.
How options 2 and 3 would behave together; this was not measured.

follow_ups.text: Remeasure the rules in force (with sanction_lambda 1) under this period's conditions to confirm the on-time gain, the customer wait monitors and Company C's utility loss.
Should Company C's utility loss under sanction_lambda 1 be addressed, for example by treating fairness between companies as part of the KPI reading?
